raw_data.lotInfo:
This lot consists of an estimated 300+ Long Tons of Government-owned scrap metals located at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers waterfront facility, 3500 Grand Avenue, Pittsburgh, PA 15225.

The property consists primarily of:

  • Plate and Structural Steel (P&S)
  • No. 1 Heavy Melting Steel (HMS #1)
  • Fabricated steel components and structural assemblies
  • Aluminum
  • Mixed ferrous and non-ferrous scrap metals
  • Scrap with incidental foreign attachments such as wood, rubber, fasteners, hardware, and other non-metallic materials

This is a one-time lump-sum sale. Removal of the property shall be performed by hopper barge only.

The Government will load the purchased property directly onto the purchaser's hopper barge(s) using Government personnel and Government-owned equipment. The purchaser is responsible for providing all barge(s), tug services, marine transportation, labor, equipment, and logistics necessary to complete removal.

The approximate heaviest individual piece is estimated to weigh up to 35 tons, and the approximate longest individual piece is estimated to be 62 feet. These dimensions are estimates provided for planning purposes only and are not warranted.

Important Dates

  • IFB Issuance: July 10, 2026
  • Deadline for Questions: August 7, 2026
  • Bid Submission Deadline: August 10, 2026, 5:00 PM Central Time
  • Public Bid Opening (Google Meet): August 12, 2026 (Time TBD)
  • Anticipated Pre-Award Notice: August 14, 2026

Mandatory Site Inspection

A mandatory site inspection is required prior to bidding. Failure to attend the mandatory site inspection will render a bidder ineligible for award.

Bidders are responsible for scheduling their inspection directly with:

Jason Shackleford
General Supply Specialist (FLO)
U.S. Army Corps of Engineers - Pittsburgh District
3500 Grand Ave
Pittsburgh, PA 15225
Office: (412) 395-7615

Inspection and removal are available Monday through Friday by confirmed appointment only. The facility is closed on Federal holidays.

This sale is conducted by sealed bid. Bidders shall submit Appendix A and Standard Form 114 by the bid deadline identified above. Appendix B shall not be submitted with the bid and will be requested only from the apparent successful bidder, if required.

CONDITION OF THE PROPERTY IS NOT WARRANTED. PHOTOGRAPHS, ESTIMATES, DESCRIPTIONS, AND OTHER REPRESENTATIONS ARE PROVIDED FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY AND ARE NOT WARRANTED.

Please review the complete Invitation for Bids (IFB), all appendices, photographs, maps, and supporting documents before scheduling a site inspection or submitting a bid.

Aircraft are not viewable on weekends or after hours. You must provide at least 5 working days advance notice of intent to visually inspect the airplane.

1978 BEECHCRAFT T-34C, BUNO 160948.

Please read the entire description carefully.

*NOTE: Both FAA return to service certification and estimated flight hours remaining are predicated on Fatigue Life Remaining, and whether Full Carry Through and AFB-70's are completed. It behooves the buyer to be cognizant of these requirements prior to bidding/acquisition, especially with respect to return to service.

The remaining hour calculations are based on the assumption that the aircraft continues to be flown at the current FLE burn rate as seen by the CNAF T-34 fleet. Aircraft remaining life drops dramatically if operators fly the aircraft to peak design limits.

AFB-70 Complete - No

Engine hours since overhaul - 1,340.9

Last major inspection, prop (phase 2) - 23 Sep 2013
Last major inspection, engine (phase 1) - 7 Feb 2014
Last major inspection, engine (phase 2) - 6 Mar 2013

Engine SERNO CE58313

Aircraft was inducted into AMARG 29 May 2014 in long-term preservation at Davis-Monthan AF base.

Bidder is responsible for funding AMARG to prepare and tow the aircraft to one of a number of MRO's just outside of the base, and is required to supply a set of aircraft tires/wheels:

Tire Specs:
Main tires are 19.5x6.75-8 P/N 196K08-9.
They are TUBELESS tires Nose wheel is 5.00-5 P/N 505C01-2 and is a TUBE type tire

Historical records are available to review/inspect at aircraft location during physical inspection. Records are provided for informational purposes only. The accuracy and availability of records are NOT guaranteed or warranted.

The removal time frame will be extended so that the End Use Certificate DLA form can be completed by the winning bidder and must be approved by the Department of War before the aircraft shall be released to the winning bidder. The End Use Certificate form is located on the "Documents" Section below.

****WARNING TO BIDDER:
-The current EUC assessment timeframe is roughly 30-60 days but could move in either direction. Payment is due within five (5) business days after the End Use Certificate receives approval.

- Upon approval of the End Use Certificate by Trade Security Controls, the winning bidder pays GSA the purchase price. Separately, since this aircraft is located in AMARG, a government contractor, additional fees will be assessed by AMARG. It is solely the responsibility of the winning bidder to complete a Statement of Work and coordinate with AMARG (Davis-Monthan Air Force Base). Additional fees will be incurred prior to removing the aircraft; the estimated cost is between $23,000 to $25,000.

Interested parties are strongly encouraged to inspect the aircraft prior to bidding or procurement. Specific engine and maintenance due questions for this aircraft are upon request. This aircraft may NOT be in compliance with applicable FAA requirements and has neither been registered with the FAA nor maintained in accordance with FAA standards. The buyer is responsible for bringing this aircraft into compliance with applicable standards by obtaining all necessary FAA inspections or modifications.

This aircraft was certified by the United States Navy (USN) and flown under Military Type Certification (MTC) for purposes of airworthiness. It is the assuming owner's responsibility to obtain airworthiness certification from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) or equivalent agency. The USN does not possess all the technical data required to obtain such certification and it is thereby incumbent upon the owner to work with the appropriate Type Certificate (TC) and Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) holders to certify and confirm the aircraft is in the configuration desired by the operator.

SOLD AS-IS/WHERE-IS without spares. All sales are final, and no warranty is implied or applied. Photographs may not depict an exact representation of the item offered and should not be relied upon in place of written item description.

The Government shall not be liable for personal injuries to, disabilities of, or death of any persons arising from or incidental to the inspection, purchase, removal, use or disposition of this aircraft. The successful bidder shall hold the Government harmless from any or all debts, liabilities, judgments, costs, demands, suits, actions, or claims of any nature arising from or incidental to inspection, purchase, use, or resale of this item. (ICN: N65965-6037-0001)

Overview

This lot contains (2) ScripTalk Talking Prescription Label Printers, Model 220-SN. The printers are classified in used condition. These are specialized network-capable label printers used in pharmacy or medical environments to produce electronic talking prescription labels that can be read aloud by compatible ScripTalk reader devices for visually or print-impaired patients.

Key Features

  • Network-capable connectivity for integration with pharmacy computer systems.
  • Designed to print to microchip-embedded label stock for electronic audio functionality.
  • Built for repeated daily use in clinical settings.
  • Compatible with ScripTalk reader devices for audio playback of prescription information.
